rationale: Round 6, ADR-conformance lens. I read 8b3a5535 from disk and reviewed `git diff 7404845f 8b3a5535`; this was read-only. All three of my round-5 asks are ADDRESSED. The finder-only F2 rule now refuses on any visible, well-formed reviewed_head_sha outside the tip, compares no rounds and grants no anchor authority, which is a simpler and stronger fit for ADR-0041. On a normal bead it does not refuse. With one review round, the reviewed SHA B is an ancestor of the merge's second parent, so it is in the tip's history (AC-11 (i-c)/(iv)). After a fix round, the in-place bump overwrites the earlier SHA, so only the landed round remains (AC-11 (i-a)). #239 still recovers through reattest (AC-11 (i)). Every F2 refusal names the one exit that can change the blocked outcome, the dependent's scoped MF-3 override, so §2(i) holds. q9ea is correctly confined to the primary-path NoEvidence arm. Against ADR-0042, the malformed-SHA provenance gate runs before any git operand, pinned by AC-11 (x-m). The residual is now exact: only F1/F3/F4 are git-derived, a panel-file edit defeats F2 with no JSONL trace, and AC-11 (ix-g) pins that reach so it cannot later be claimed closed. I verified that reviews/ is untracked on this branch (`git ls-tree` at 8b3a5535 shows only spec.md under the spec dir), while 59 finished-spec panel.json files are tracked. AC-18's text-pin enumerates every element of the amendment. One wording nit remains in the residual bullets, which AC-18 will carry into the ADR text.
concrete_changes_required: R4.2 Residual wording: one bullet says the panel-edit forge 'is the same class as a forged exact-match reviewed_head_sha confirming a primary-path candidate under Spec-125 item (c)', and the next says the reach 'is a new, bounded reach, not "the same class"'. Because AC-18 pins this text into ADR-0041, make the distinction explicit: 'same forge MECHANISM as Spec-125 item (c) (agent-writable panel data); NEW REACH (undirected off-first-parent merges that Spec 125 fails today)'.

findings.title: Finder-only F2 + exact residual in the ADR-0041 amendment (AC-18) — judged
findings.detail: AC-18 now requires the amendment to name: F1–F5 with each one's provenance (F1/F3/F4 from git, F2 from untracked agent-writable panel files); F2's no-round-comparison rule; abandoned and malformed-SHA handling and the visibility limit; the audited tuple, its validity contract and the validity-qualified no-op; the provenance string; q9ea's exclusion; the metadata-forge and panel-edit residuals; the read-back conditions; the undirected-subject gap; the non-corroborating panel datum and its CLOSE reach; the binding veto vs audited repair; and the scoped fingerprinted override. This is consistent with ADR-0041 §2(i) (a genuine exit on every refusal), §2(ii) (CLOSE paths first-parent; never subject text alone; nothing automatic on a fallback), and the Spec-125 audit rule (before/after keys plus the accepted tuple and provenance, recorded on every acceptance including the validity-qualified no-op). It is also consistent with ADR-0037 §8 (panel data unauthenticated, residual stated) and ADR-0042 (wellFormedGitObjectID before any git operand).

findings.title: Does 'any outside-tip registration refuses' refuse a normal bead? Does #239 still recover?
findings.detail: Normal bead, one round: reviewed B is the second parent or its ancestor (complete's later commits sit between them), so B is in the tip's history and F2 passes (AC-11 (i-c)). Normal bead with a fix round: the in-place bump overwrites the earlier SHA, which matches the BRIEF's evidence of 59 registrations and no `-r*` dirs, so F2 passes (AC-11 (i-a)). #239: a single landed registration passes F2, reattest accepts, and MF-3 then passes via the audited tuple (AC-11 (i)). Refusing cases are fail-closed by design: a `-r2` directory beside a rebased-away predecessor, cross-directory rounds, and abandoned outside-tip registrations. Each names the R6 exit, so none is a §2(i) deadlock. Residual edge: a bead branch rewritten after review but before landing (a rebase rather than a merge) refuses. mindspec merges and does not rebase bead branches, and the R6 exit applies.

findings.title: Residual bullets say both 'same class' and 'not the same class'
findings.detail: R4.2: 'It is the same class as a forged exact-match reviewed_head_sha confirming a primary-path candidate under Spec-125 item (c)' is followed by 'It is a new, bounded reach, not "the same class".' The two are about different things (mechanism vs reach), but the text, which AC-18 pins into ADR-0041, reads as self-contradictory.

findings.title: Errors in this BRIEF
findings.detail: (1) The machine header (lines 11–12) still says to write '<your-slot>-round-6.json beside this BRIEF'. The 'Verdict location' override section corrects it. (2) Small evidence-count mismatch: the BRIEF's Round-6 section says '59 registrations on main', while the spec says 'A panel slot verified 48 registrations at round ≥ 2'. Both can be true (59 total, 48 at round ≥ 2), but the spec should name the total so the two numbers cannot be read as conflicting.
